exposure: Read under the D14 exception: tools/audit/bugclasses.json; git commit messages and stats for 3511677a, c4f8f213, e299cd72, 8e5d1ace, b64c2f8c, df6e55f8, fd1a8528, 93e3af05, 2a451021, 1e4e4b9e and 8c3a13c4; git-archive trees at 3511677a, b64c2f8c, e299cd72, 1e4e4b9e and 8c3a13c4 and their parents (the instances' pre- and post-fix code). Also read the in-tree barrier tests/finite_boundary.py. No tools/audit/round3..8 evidence file was opened; one commit --stat listed a filename under tools/audit/round5/ and it is not cited. No gh or GitHub was used.

coverage.evidence: bugclasses.json: P1 has 12 instances over rounds 1-6 and P6 has 18 over rounds 1-4, 6 and 7. Both are status open with detector and barrier null. Instance histories were traced in git (commit list in exposure).
The scope assigns P1 and P6. P1 has a partial in-tree barrier (QuarantiningStore plus tests/finite_boundary.py) covering non-finite numeric leaves only; P6 has no enumerating detector.

p1_store.py covers 13 stores and 4027 mutants through real loaders, consumers and a 3-cycle wedge arm; its clean fixture is 0. p6_keys.py has arms A (recording coordinator.data over 5 topologies x 2 cycles), B (entity ids) and C (getattr on undefined names); its self-test and clean fixture give 1 and 0. Both re-find instances at pre-fix trees: 3511677a^ (R1 D1-01, D1-05), b64c2f8c^ (R5 D1-05/06, poison 453->410), e299cd72^ (R6 D1-01/02, 410->0), 1e4e4b9e^ (R7 D8-01, 6->2), 8c3a13c4^ (R6 D6-02, 2->0). Both move under a one-line re-introduction.
One finding per class, D14-s1-01 (P1) and D14-s1-02 (P6). Each states the property, the detector command and every seam the detector lists at baseline.

A barrier location and fix scope are proposed for each class. The gate cost is provisional: p1_store 22-26 s wall and p6_keys about 10 s, single-threaded, at load1 1.2-2.5. Nothing was landed in tests/.

unfinished.what: P6 card arm: the attributes the card JS (www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js) reads against the attributes entities publish, e.g. via a Proxy over card_rig states. Not built.
P1 type-drift arm: a malformed bool or str leaf that loads as a wrong value without raising, e.g. away.restore_override's bool(raw.get('active')) takes the string 'false' as True. Not measured.
The barrier is proposed and costed but not implemented in tests/, and its wall cost needs a quiet-window re-take.

findings.title: P1: a malformed store leaf raises out of a loader or consumer; a naive legionella timestamp wedges every refresh
findings.claim: At baseline, 11 of 4027 single-leaf store mutants (7 seams) raise out of a real loader or consumer. A naive timestamp in dhw_legionella fails 3 of 3 _async_update_data cycles, and none of the 7 seams falls on a leaf that tests/finite_boundary.py substitutes.
findings.mechanism: QuarantiningStore scrubs only non-finite numeric leaves, and finite_boundary.py substitutes only numeric leaves and drives only the loader and _build_data_dict. Stored timestamps are parsed without awareness coercion and compared with the aware dt_util.now(). best_restore calls np.isfinite on an arbitrary leaf, _apply_learner_payloads assumes learners is a dict, and pump_arbiter._load assumes the shape of written.

findings.title: P6: horizon_hours read from coordinator.data but never written; boost probes a field only a test double defines
findings.claim: At baseline, 2 consumer reads of coordinator.data (sensor.py:1482 and :1515, key horizon_hours) are absent in all 10 driven cells and written by no producer, and 1 getattr (boost.py:212 boost_calls) probes a name only tests/harness.py:FakeCoordinator defines.
findings.mechanism: The plan sensors publish horizon_hours via data.get('horizon_hours', 24.0), but _build_data_dict never writes it; the value comes from the fallback, which equals the never-assigned OptimizationConfig.horizon_hours default only by coincidence. boost.set_channel skips persist() whenever the coordinator carries a boost_calls recorder, which only the test double does.

leads.what: The stub returns a naive datetime.now() when no clock is frozen, while Home Assistant's dt_util.now() is always aware. Tests on the default clock therefore never compare an aware stored timestamp with an aware now, and never meet the naive-stored case that production meets (class P11, which no round-9 seat's axis holds).
